sentences.text: This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is arrayed as the 4 th accused in Crime No.21 of 2023 of Koipuram Police Station,
Pathanamthitta.
He apprehends arrest in the above crime.
Though this bail applications was filed in March, 2025, it was not brought up till date, since it is pointed out by the learned Public Prosecutor that petitioner was all along outside the country.
However, the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that petitioner is now in Kerala and therefore this bail application can be considered.

3. Petitioner and other accused are alleged to have been part of a company by name PRD Mini Nidhi Limited and they had cheated the defacto complainants by collecting large amount of money after promising to pay interest and return the amount on its maturity.

Subsequently, they failed to pay either the interest or return the amount and thereby committed the offences under 2025:KER:51922 Sections 409 and 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, apart from Sections 3 and 5 of the Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019 (for short, the 'BUDS Act').
4.

entities.text: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that petitioner had no role in the day to day management of the affairs of the company as he was made a Director by the first accused, who is his father and also, since he was all along residing in Singapore, having no role at all in the conduct of business.
According to the learned counsel, the first accused has already been arrested and hence petitioner's custodial interrogation is not at all necessary.
It was further submitted that petitioner is willing to abide by any condition that may be imposed.
Reliance was also placed on the order of this Court dated 26.03.2025 in BA.No.3872 of 2025 and connected cases.
It was submitted that in all similar matters, petitioner has been granted anticipatory bail, subject to conditions.

5. The learned Public Prosecutor, on the other hand, opposed the application and submitted that since the offence alleged against the petitioner and other accused are serious, custodial interrogation is necessary.

It was also submitted that petitioner remained aloof from investigation in all these cases and it was only after anticipatory bail was granted to him in BA.No.3872 of 2025 and connected cases that petitioner came 2025:KER:51922 down to Kerala.
6.
I have considered the rival contentions.
7. Petitioner is the 4th accused in the crime.
He is alleged to have been the Director of PRD Mini Nidhi Limited of which his father is the Managing Director who is arrayed as the first accused.

Since petitioner contended that he is settled in Singapore and was not attending the day to day affairs of the company and further that he went abroad in 2019, a learned single Judge of this Court had granted anticipatory bail in BA.No.3872 of 2025 and connected cases.

Those cases relate to similar Anantha Krishnan vs State Of Kerala on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90453504/
2 crimes registered at the behest of other complainants.
8.

sentences.text: Taking note of the aforesaid order, which is produced as Annexure A3 in BA.No.4730 of 2025, I am of the view that a different view need not be adopted in the instant case since the allegations are similar and also since it was on behalf of petitioner submitted that he is ready to abide by any conditions imposed by the Court.

9. In Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another [(2020) 5 SCC 1], it was held that while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail or not, Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant,
and the 2025:KER:51922 facts of the case.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal and Others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and Another [(2020) 5 SCC 1]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Grant of anticipatory bail is a matter of discretion and the kind of conditions to be imposed or not to be imposed all dependent on facts of each case, and subject to the discretion of the court.
10. I am satisfied that custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not necessary in the instant crime.
However, since petitioner's presence for interrogation is necessary, he shall subject himself to interrogation.

11. Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions :
(a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 28.07.2025 and shall subject himself to interrogation.

(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioner,
then, he shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.
(d) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall he tamper with the evidence.
(e) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the 2025:KER:51922 jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.
